Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business coverage across outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which has triggered a board investigation, a stock selloff, and congressional scrutiny over AI chip export policy. Markets are also digesting a brutal tech/AI stock rout, falling oil prices amid hopes of Iran de-escalation, and ripple effects from the Democratic midterm sweep on Fed and bank regulation.

stories.headline: Nvidia board investigates CEO Jensen Huang over affair with suspected Chinese spy
stories.summary: Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive U.S. intelligence believes was recruited by China's spy agency, sending Nvidia shares down roughly 5% and raising 'key man risk' questions for the AI industry.

stories.headline: Wall Street tries to shrug off historic AI stock rout
stories.summary: US stocks opened higher Monday as dip-buyers scooped up beaten-down tech shares following the S&P 500's worst week since April 2025, even as hedge funds had dumped technology stocks at one of the fastest paces on record.

stories.headline: Oil extends slide as Iran diplomacy hopes grow
stories.summary: Oil prices fell further as optimism mounted over diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East conflict, after Trump told CNN that further strikes on Iran were unlikely while nuclear and Strait of Hormuz negotiations continue.

stories.headline: SoftBank's massive AI bet under pressure from tech sell-off
stories.summary: Founder Masayoshi Son faces falling valuations across SoftBank's AI holdings ahead of an upcoming earnings report, as the broader tech rout tests the sustainability of his aggressive AI wager.

stories.headline: Paraguay bank collapse ensnares sitting president
stories.summary: Prosecutors have accused Paraguayan President Santiago Peña of funneling nearly a billion dollars of government funds to the Ueno bank as its executives made reckless insider loans that led to its implosion.

stories.headline: Why 95-year-old law firm Weil Gotshal collapsed despite being profitable
stories.summary: Weil Gotshal's downfall stemmed from a failure to adapt to Big Law's increasingly cutthroat, eat-or-be-eaten competitive culture even as the firm remained profitable.

stories.headline: No record of Trump-Warsh call raises questions over Fed influence claims
stories.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's September calendar did not reflect a conversation that President Trump said he had with him about how to vote at a Federal Reserve meeting.

stories.headline: Foreign buyers have snapped up half a trillion pounds of British companies
stories.summary: An FT analysis finds that companies worth roughly half a trillion pounds have been acquired by foreign buyers over the past decade, underscoring concerns about Britain's shrinking corporate base.

Business.gaps: Puck had no business-relevant items visible in search results or feed; Business Insider and Politico's business-specific coverage could not be independently verified beyond what appeared in the general feed (Politico items skewed toward midterm politics rather than business).

US politics.overview: Coverage across these outlets is dominated by the fallout from Democrats' sweeping midterm victory: a tense lame-duck Congress, a Trump White House shake-up, and intra-party reckonings in both parties over 2028. Secondary but fast-moving threads include the Jensen Huang/Nvidia espionage scandal and Supreme Court developments including a reheating Dobbs leak probe.

stories.headline: Congress returns for a volatile lame-duck session with Hegseth impeachment push and shutdown looming
stories.summary: Lawmakers are back in Washington facing a Dec. 11 funding deadline, with Punchbowl reporting that odds of a shutdown have risen sharply as Democrats weigh whether to use the Iran war as leverage, while Jeffries and Schumer huddle privately on strategy.

stories.headline: Trump reshuffles inner circle, names Stephen Miller chief of staff after midterm drubbing
stories.summary: NPR reports Trump is overhauling his senior team following Democrats' huge midterm gains, signaling he intends to confront a divided government aggressively rather than moderate course; The Dispatch's morning newsletter also flagged Miller's elevation to chief of staff.

stories.headline: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over alleged ties to accused Chinese spy
stories.summary: Courthouse News reports Nvidia is investigating whether Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence after he acknowledged an intimate relationship with a business executive U.S. intelligence believes was gathering information for Beijing; Trump called Huang an "honorable guy" despite the allegations, and Nvidia shares fell more than 5% in premarket trading.

stories.headline: Senate Republicans return to Capitol furious with Trump after midterm losses
stories.summary: The Hill reports Senate Republicans returning to Washington are openly blaming President Trump for last week's big losses in Senate and House races, with anger raising questions about the party's direction; Axios similarly described Trump as "defiant" and entering a lame-duck era despite the setbacks.

stories.headline: JD Vance's 2028 standing clouded after blaming GOP losses on Iran war
stories.summary: NPR reports Vice President Vance is trying to recast his political future after the GOP's historic wipeout, having publicly blamed the Iran war for the losses; The Hill noted Trump said "a lot of people didn't like" Vance's comments, while Washington Examiner is probing whether Vance privately thinks Trump was wrong to attack Iran.

stories.headline: Progressive bloc of incoming Democrats won't commit to Jeffries as speaker
stories.summary: The Washington Examiner reports the incoming House Democratic class's progressive wing is stopping short of committing to Hakeem Jeffries for speaker, signaling an early intraparty fight even as he is widely expected to win; Punchbowl similarly reported a DSA-aligned member demanding concessions on Medicare for All and Israel policy before backing him.

stories.headline: DOJ ramps up criminal probe into the Dobbs leak as Schumer vows to block "right-winger" SCOTUS picks
stories.summary: SCOTUSblog reports the Justice Department has intensified its criminal investigation into who leaked the 2022 abortion draft opinion, even as the court heard arguments in a religious-discrimination case over Catholic preschools and Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said Democrats will not allow Trump to install "a right-winger" on the court.

stories.headline: Democratic landslide flips state legislative power nationwide
stories.summary: Politico reports Democrats picked up more than 500 state legislative seats and flipped at least a dozen chambers in last week's elections, reshaping the map of state power ahead of 2028.

US politics.gaps: Cook Political Report had no recent items surfacing in search; NYT, WSJ and The Guardian block search so only their provided feed items (on AI-in-schools, Nvidia, Fed chief calendar dispute, and election volatility) could be used.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which has triggered a board investigation, a stock selloff, and questions about his future. A secondary cluster of stories covers the political aftershocks of the US midterms for AI policy and data centers, plus competitive moves in the AI chip and model race from Google, Anthropic, and Apple.

stories.headline: Nvidia opens investigation into Jensen Huang's ties to suspected Chinese spy
stories.summary: Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who US officials believe was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on him; the scandal has already wiped billions off Nvidia's market value and raised questions about whether Huang can keep his job.

stories.headline: Democrats' midterm sweep puts AI data centers and chip exports in the crosshairs
stories.summary: With Democrats taking both chambers of Congress, VentureBeat reports a near-total nationwide backlash against data centers at the ballot box and a push for stronger AI oversight, transparency rules, and kill-switch legislation, even as the party lacks a unified stance on how far to go.

stories.headline: Google ships two new specialized TPUs to challenge Nvidia
stories.summary: Google is expanding its TPU lineup with the encrypted-data TPU 8tx and the higher-compute TPU 8i Max for long-context tasks, intensifying its push to compete directly with Nvidia in AI chips.

stories.headline: Anthropic pushes ahead with IPO despite tech selloff, at a lower valuation
stories.summary: Anthropic is moving forward with a pre-Thanksgiving IPO targeting a $1.25 to $1.75 trillion valuation, well below its earlier $2 trillion goal, as the broader AI stock rout weighs on investor appetite.

stories.headline: Apple accelerates push to make Siri more agentic
stories.summary: Citing Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, The Verge reports that Apple CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI chief Craig Federighi to speed up Siri's roadmap toward a more powerful AI agent to compete with OpenAI's offerings.

stories.headline: Chinese AI labs struggle to lure Silicon Valley talent despite aggressive recruiting
stories.summary: Chinese startups like MiniMax and Moonshot are opening US outposts to recruit top engineers, but pay gaps, prestige differences, and national-security tensions are making it difficult to pull talent away from OpenAI and Anthropic.

stories.headline: Meta expands Instagram's AI age-detection tool globally
stories.summary: Meta is rolling out its AI age-estimation technology worldwide to catch teenagers on Instagram who misstated their age, automatically placing more minors under Teen Account safety restrictions.

stories.headline: AI stock rout stabilizes as dip-buyers step back in
stories.summary: US stocks opened the week firmer as investors bought back into beaten-down tech shares following the S&P 500's worst week since early 2025, even as Nvidia's spy scandal added fresh pressure on the sector.

Tech & AI.gaps: The Information, IEEE Spectrum, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind had no distinct recent stories surfaced beyond what's referenced above (Anthropic's IPO news came via The Decoder, not Anthropic's own site). Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist, Guardian, and The Verge results reflect feed items only, since these outlets block broader search.

Energy.overview: Coverage is dominated by the opening of the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, where organizers are pushing a global electrification target amid a geopolitically fraught backdrop, alongside intertwined US stories on oil-market jitters tied to Iran diplomacy, Europe's gas-storage squeeze, and the US permitting-reform push colliding with the Trump administration's continued offshore wind attacks. Energy-specialist outlets (Latitude Media, Canary Media, Heatmap) are also focused heavily on how last week's US midterm results are reshaping data-center and utility politics.

stories.headline: COP31 Opens in Antalya With Narrower Agenda and Shrinking Climate Ambitions
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that negotiators from nearly 200 countries are convening in Antalya under a narrower agenda than any COP since Paris, though the energy crisis and an AI backlash could still spur new action; the summit's main push is a 'presidency-led' pledge to raise electricity's share of final energy demand to 35% by 2035.

stories.headline: Oil Extends Drop on Hopes of Diplomatic Progress to End Middle East War
stories.summary: Oil prices fell further as optimism grew over diplomatic efforts to end the regional war, even though fighting continues, with an unconfirmed report that Iran eased its Hormuz-related demands adding to the move; WSJ separately reported Trump downplaying the odds of new strikes on Iran.

stories.headline: Europe's Gas Storage Problems Seen Lasting Well Beyond Winter
stories.summary: Bloomberg's energy newsletter warns that European gas inventories could fall to their lowest level in more than a decade by spring, signaling a storage shortfall that outlasts the current winter heating season.

stories.headline: Revolution Wind Reaches Full Power Despite Trump Administration's Repeated Attacks
stories.summary: Canary Media reports that Ørsted's 704-megawatt Revolution Wind project off Connecticut and Rhode Island is now fully operational, becoming the third US utility-scale offshore wind farm to reach commercial operation despite stop-work orders and ongoing litigation from the Interior Department.

stories.headline: Trump's Renewed Offshore Wind Attacks Threaten to Derail Bipartisan Permitting Deal
stories.summary: Canary Media details how the Senate's bipartisan permitting bill, which could cut years off transmission and energy-project timelines, is being jeopardized after the administration asked courts to reconsider permits for New England Wind and other offshore projects, prompting one sponsoring senator to warn it could 'blow up' negotiations.

stories.headline: Midterm Results Show Voters Rebuking Utilities and Data Centers Over Rate Hikes
stories.summary: Latitude Media's post-election coverage finds that voters in Georgia and Michigan punished utilities over rate hikes and political spending, while candidates who opposed data centers performed well, signaling a shift in energy-affordability politics heading into 2027.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches 'Grid Protection Program' to Ease Data Center Power Concerns
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports that OpenAI is rolling out a non-binding program to work with utilities on demand response and flexibility at its data center campuses, starting with its 3.2-gigawatt Project Camellia in Georgia, as public backlash over data-center power demands grows.

Energy.gaps: No recent coverage could be found from Argus Media or E&E News within the last 48 hours (only older archived articles appeared in search). FT, WSJ, NYT and The Economist block web search, so only their provided feed items were used, which were limited mostly to oil-market and general-news items rather than dedicated energy/climate features.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage this period is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission of an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence suspects of spying for China, a story with major implications for the upcoming Trump-Xi APEC summit. Alongside that, outlets are tracking fresh signs of strain in China's economy (accelerating factory-gate inflation, stock-market stabilization efforts), a sharp slowdown in China's EV market, and renewed US-China trade friction and Taiwan security concerns ahead of this month's APEC meetings.

stories.headline: Nvidia board probes CEO Jensen Huang after he admits affair with alleged Chinese spy
stories.summary: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation into Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman U.S. officials say was working for Chinese intelligence, a scandal that has hit the stock and could complicate Trump's planned APEC meeting with Xi Jinping; state-run Global Times quoted China's foreign ministry spokesperson calling the spy claims "completely groundless and... nothing but a smear against China."

stories.headline: China's factory-gate inflation hits highest level in more than four years
stories.summary: China's producer price index rose 5.7% year-on-year in October, the fastest pace since June 2022, driven largely by energy costs, even as consumer inflation slowed to 0.7%, highlighting a widening gap between upstream and downstream prices.

stories.headline: Top US, China officials raise trade 'concerns' ahead of APEC summit
stories.summary: Senior US and Chinese officials held frank talks on trade tensions ahead of an Asia-Pacific summit in China this month where their leaders are expected to meet; Nikkei Asia separately reported Washington pressing Beijing on rare-earth export commitments and farm-goods purchases.

stories.headline: China's NEV sales fall for 10th straight month as Tesla and BYD diverge sharply
stories.summary: China's NEV retail sales fell 13.7% in October even as penetration hit a record 67.5%, while Tesla's China retail sales sank to their lowest since mid-2022 (down 66% year-on-year) and BYD hit a 19-million-unit production milestone, underscoring how price competition is reshaping the market.

stories.headline: Beijing pushes to stabilize capital markets as State Council meets
stories.summary: China's State Council, chaired by Premier Li Qiang, called for stronger mechanisms to stabilize capital markets and told authorities to make full use of policy funding and pay businesses promptly, while Vice Premier He Lifeng separately raised concerns over U.S. trade restrictions.

stories.headline: Chinese AI labs try to poach Silicon Valley engineers from OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.summary: Chinese startups including MiniMax and Moonshot are opening U.S. outposts to recruit American AI talent, but face steep pay gaps, weaker prestige, and national-security scrutiny that make luring engineers away from leading U.S. labs difficult.

stories.headline: Taiwan's security council tightens anti-infiltration measures
stories.summary: Taiwan's National Security Council has moved to tighten measures against infiltration, part of a broader push reported by Taipei Times that also includes harsher penalties being planned for collaborators and new restrictions on Chinese-owned yachts at Taiwan ports.

stories.headline: China's renminbi trade strategy aims to 'de-weaponize' the dollar, not replace it
stories.summary: The Wire China argues that Beijing's expanding renminbi-based trade with countries like Russia and Iran is less about dethroning the dollar globally and more about insulating itself and partners from U.S. financial leverage.

China.gaps: No recent China-specific coverage was found via search for Sixth Tone, China Media Project, China Daily, Xinhua, CGTN, or Yicai Global in this window.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the fallout from Sunday's Houthi missile and drone attack that damaged Saudi Aramco's tower in Riyadh's financial district, alongside intensifying but inconclusive US-Iran diplomacy after Trump's Monday meeting with Qatar's prime minister. Parallel coverage focuses on Gadi Eisenkot's fraught attempt to form Israel's next government, Syria's expanding security role alongside Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, and growing business/economic jitters tied to the broader Iran war, including falling oil prices and disrupted flights and corporate plans in the Gulf.

stories.headline: Houthi missile and drone barrage damages Aramco tower in Riyadh's financial district
stories.summary: A Houthi missile and drone attack on Sunday blew out windows across multiple floors of the Aramco Tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, with no injuries reported but business and travel disruption continuing into Monday as offices and flights remained affected. The strike, which also reportedly targeted Riyadh airport and Aramco facilities in Abqaiq, is seen by analysts as a major escalation threatening confidence in Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 economic transformation.

stories.headline: Trump meets Qatari PM as US-Iran talks edge forward with no deal imminent
stories.summary: President Trump held closed-door talks with Qatar's prime minister as mediation efforts to end the Iran war intensify, though Washington and Tehran remain divided over Iran's demands and the terms for ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Trump separately said a resumption of strikes was "highly unlikely" if negotiations progress, while Secretary of State Rubio cautioned there was no breakthrough yet and called some Iranian demands "outrageous."

stories.headline: Eisenkot begins fraught push to form Israeli government, outmaneuvering Netanyahu
stories.summary: Former army chief Gadi Eisenkot received the mandate from President Herzog to try to form Israel's next government after winning 67 Knesset recommendations to Netanyahu's 46, but faces a narrow path given splits between his Jewish-led and Arab-led backers over Haredi conscription and reliance on Arab parties. Haredi parties such as UTJ and Shas are being courted as potential kingmakers, while Netanyahu has called for a "unity government" that Eisenkot has so far rejected.

stories.headline: Oil prices slide as diplomatic hopes on Iran grow
stories.summary: Oil extended losses as markets priced in optimism over diplomatic progress toward ending the Iran war, even as attacks in the region continued, with Brent seen facing further downward pressure if de-escalation holds. Trump's comments downplaying the likelihood of renewed strikes on Iran, tied to progress on Hormuz and nuclear talks, were cited as the main driver of the roughly 3% drop.

stories.headline: UAE's Gargash warns region faces prolonged uncertainty as US-Iran deal remains elusive
stories.summary: Senior Emirati official Anwar Gargash told an Abu Dhabi conference that a comprehensive US-Iran political settlement looks difficult and that the region should brace for a long period in which neither a decisive resolution nor a stable order can be assumed. He said the war's consequences may persist, requiring the UAE to keep investing in defensive capabilities and deterrence alongside international partners.

stories.headline: Syria's expanding security role alongside Saudi Arabia against the Houthis draws scrutiny
stories.summary: Syrian officials publicly deny sending troops to fight in Yemen, even as reports and apparent security integration suggest Damascus forces are being deployed alongside Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, with analysts linking the move to a possible Syrian-Saudi defense pact reshaping regional power dynamics. The denials come as Yemeni officials told reporters thousands of Syrian troops were already on the ground.

stories.headline: Egypt train crash kills seven, injures over 100, prompting calls for transport minister's resignation
stories.summary: A collision between two trains in Egypt's Giza killed at least seven people and injured more than 114, triggering public pressure for the transport minister to step down over the latest in a string of rail accidents.

stories.headline: QatarEnergy expands Africa push with Namibia offshore stake
stories.summary: QatarEnergy agreed to acquire a 25% stake in an offshore oil block in Namibia, part of its continued push to expand its international upstream portfolio beyond its core LNG business.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Arab News, Gulf News, Arabian Business, Zawya, Al Arabiya English, Ynetnews, and Haaretz did not surface distinct recent lead stories in search results within the allowed window; BBC, Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, and The Economist were only available via the provided feed items since they block web search.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage this week centers on South Africa's historic ANC election collapse, legal and political turmoil in Tanzania and Sudan, and a cluster of economic stories on African borrowing costs, crypto regulation and the scramble for critical minerals. Business-focused outlets (TechCabal, The Africa Report, Mining Weekly, African Business) are also tracking Nigeria's crypto/stablecoin crackdown, DRC's push to convert its US minerals pact into real investment, and oil majors retreating from African refining as Dangote expands.

stories.headline: ANC suffers worst-ever election result in South Africa
stories.summary: Final tallies from Sunday's local elections showed the African National Congress winning just 31% of the vote, its weakest showing since the end of apartheid, intensifying fragmentation of South Africa's political order. Africa Confidential and African Business both flagged the result as potentially reshaping the national coalition and empowering political brokers.

stories.headline: Tanzania opposition leader Lissu convicted of incitement after treason acquittal
stories.summary: A Dar es Salaam court acquitted opposition figure Tundu Lissu of treason but handed him a four-year sentence for incitement, a split verdict that keeps alive the political confrontation over President Samia's human-rights record, as Mo Ibrahim Foundation governance reports warn of rising authoritarianism in East Africa.

stories.headline: Seven killed, 125 injured in Egypt train collision
stories.summary: Two passenger trains collided south of Cairo, killing seven people and injuring at least 125, with rail workers beginning repairs to the damaged tracks in Al-Ayyat the following day.

stories.headline: Congo presses US to turn minerals pact into real investment
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's economy minister said the success of its strategic minerals partnership with Washington should be judged by completed projects rather than signed agreements, after a Paris steering-committee meeting that produced no new investment commitments.

stories.headline: Oil majors retreat from African refining as Dangote expands
stories.summary: Despite record refining margins from the Middle East conflict, international oil majors are declining to invest in African refining capacity, a gap that Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote's refinery is moving to fill.

stories.headline: Sudanese teachers strike over unpaid, inadequate wages
stories.summary: Teachers across Sudan walked out over pay they say no longer covers basic living costs, compounding the strain on a school system already battered by conflict and dilapidated infrastructure.

stories.headline: Nigeria tightens stablecoin and crypto rules as it drafts new digital-asset rulebook
stories.summary: Nigeria's regulators are moving to tighten stablecoin oversight and finalize a new digital-asset rulebook after the country lost its status as Africa's largest crypto market, with officials aiming for rules that invite innovation while closing loopholes.

stories.headline: Fears grow of resurgent piracy in the Gulf of Aden
stories.summary: Regional conflicts are fueling concern about a piracy resurgence off the Horn of Africa, prompting the EU's Operation Atalanta to deploy a frigate carrying more than 200 sailors, including a specialized team trained to retake hijacked vessels.

Africa.gaps: Reuters, AP, BBC, FT and NYT block direct search, so coverage from them is limited to the single WSJ feed item provided; no fresh African-focused items were found from those outlets beyond what was supplied.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past two days is dominated by post-midterm reckoning inside legacy newsrooms (CBS, Fox, CNN) and renewed scrutiny of AI's relationship with publishers, from Meta's scraping terms to a possible blockbuster NYT-OpenAI settlement. Business-side news includes a major streaming/audio executive shuffle at SiriusXM and continued fallout from the Russell Brand criminal trial in the UK.

stories.headline: Misread Mandate: media moguls who capitulated to Trump face a reckoning
stories.summary: CJR argues that the Democrats' midterm landslide exposes how badly media owners like the Ellison family misjudged Trump's mandate, noting the "easy capitulation of media moguls always smelled rotten" and that it now also looks absurd given the election results.

stories.headline: SiriusXM taps Tubi's Anjali Sud as new CEO
stories.summary: SiriusXM has named former Tubi chief Anjali Sud as its new CEO effective January 1, replacing Jennifer Witz, in a bet that her streaming experience can reshape the satellite-radio giant.

stories.headline: What could the NYT buy with a potential AI settlement windfall?
stories.summary: Puck reports that as reply briefs close November 20 in the Times' copyright suit against OpenAI and Microsoft, legal experts increasingly expect a settlement that could exceed a billion dollars, with one telling Puck that "news publishers have a stronger case against OpenAI than anyone."

stories.headline: Meta pulls down controversial scraping terms of service after global pushback
stories.summary: Meta has indefinitely delayed proposed commercial terms that would have let it scrape content from Meta Business accounts, telling Nieman Lab it is "pausing the changes as we continue to engage with stakeholders," after courts in Norway and Brazil blocked the terms and the UK's competition regulator opened a formal probe.

stories.headline: Major AI firms agree to common publisher opt-out signal for scraping
stories.summary: Digiday examines a new industry-backed AI training opt-out standard that major AI companies are supporting, even as it exposes deeper tensions over how aggressively AI firms scrape publisher content; Nieman Lab separately reported that Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Microsoft will support a common robots.txt-style signal letting publishers opt out of multiple AI crawlers at once.

stories.headline: Fox News ratings sink as Trump's political fortunes fade, Murdochs face a reckoning
stories.summary: State-run-adjacent note not applicable here; Status, citing Nielsen data it obtained, reports that with Trump's approval ratings near record lows, Fox News viewership is on track to decline by a striking margin even as rivals CNN and MS NOW post gains ahead of the midterms.

stories.headline: NBC's 'Kornacki Cam' outperforms rivals and rising streamers on election night
stories.summary: Puck reports that NBC's secondary "Kornacki Cam" feed was the most-watched election livestream on YouTube with more than 6 million views and 29 million views across platforms, showing that "legacy media remains oddly core to the broader platform shift" even as creators like Hasan Piker drew large audiences watching alongside it.

stories.headline: Russell Brand sexual-assault survivor accuses Channel 4 of burying her complaint
stories.summary: A woman who says she was sexually assaulted by Russell Brand while working for Channel 4 has publicly criticized the UK broadcaster for brushing her complaint "under the carpet," following his guilty verdict in the criminal trial.

Media.gaps: Could not retrieve any recent, on-topic coverage from NYT, WSJ, FT, or The Guardian beyond the single WSJ oil-markets item in the feed, since these outlets block web search and no media-industry feed items were supplied for them.
